title: EMR, Flink & OpenSearch for Big Data Compute
summary: Managed Spark, Hadoop, stream processing and log analytics clusters, serverless or provisioned.
services: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
tldr: **Amazon EMR** runs open-source Spark, Hive, HBase, Presto/Trino and Hadoop with minimal code changes. It's the answer for "lift our Hadoop cluster and keep the frameworks".
**EMR Serverless** runs Spark and Hive jobs without choosing instances or managing clusters; you pay per job. Use it for irregular jobs with nothing running in between.

**Managed Service for Apache Flink** (formerly Kinesis Data Analytics) does stateful stream processing on Kinesis or MSK. **OpenSearch Service** (successor to Amazon Elasticsearch Service) is for full-text search and log analytics.

keyFacts.text: EMR has **primary**, **core** (compute + HDFS) and **task** (compute only) nodes. Task nodes hold no HDFS data, so they are the safe place for **Spot Instances**.
EMR clusters can read and write Amazon S3 directly, so data outlives the cluster. That makes **transient clusters** per job a common cost pattern.
OpenSearch Service storage tiers. An **Index State Management** policy moves aging indexes down the tiers automatically to cut cost.
**OpenSearch Serverless** uses collections (search, time series, vector search) and scales capacity itself: no instance types, shards or capacity planning.
The **DynamoDB zero-ETL integration with OpenSearch Service** keeps a search index in sync without Streams-plus-Lambda code.

traps: Running Flink yourself on EMR works but is never the "least operational overhead" answer when Managed Service for Apache Flink fits.
Lambda tumbling windows can't do sliding windows or hold large per-key state reliably.
Athena is serverless SQL over S3, not a replacement for HBase low-latency lookups or Spark jobs with custom JARs.
Putting HDFS data on Spot core nodes risks data loss; for clusters that must finish, keep primary and core On-Demand and add Spot task nodes.
A long-lived EMR cluster sized for the biggest job wastes money when jobs are occasional; use EMR Serverless or transient clusters.
